correlate.executive_summary: The assessment discovered an exposed /ftp directory containing multiple files (including what appears to be a KeePass database) and several web security misconfigurations. A permissive CORS policy (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) and missing Content Security Policy increase the risk of data exfiltration and client-side attacks. Service enumeration revealed Apache httpd 2.4.62 on :8080 and multiple open services/ports; no NVD CVE matches could be validated during lookup. Overall, the most urgent issue is the exposed /ftp content which could disclose sensitive secrets or artifacts.

findings.title: Exposed /ftp directory with potentially sensitive files
findings.evidence: recon: HTTP 200 on /ftp (confirmed discoverable path). va (zap): multiple /ftp files listed in scanner output (e.g. /ftp/incident-support.kdbx, /ftp/encrypt.pyc, /ftp/package-lock.json.bak, /ftp/quarantine/juicy_malware_windows_64.exe.url). va (nikto): /ftp/ listed as interesting and robots.txt references /ftp. Observations from recon and VA scanners corroborate public exposure of many files.

findings.title: CORS misconfiguration allowing any origin and permissive methods
findings.evidence: va (nikto): response contained header 'access-control-allow-origin: *' and 'access-control-allow-methods: GET,HEAD,PUT,PATCH,POST,DELETE'. va (zap): Cross-Domain Misconfiguration flagged across many endpoints. Multiple scanner outputs confirm a permissive CORS configuration.

findings.title: Content Security Policy (CSP) header not set
findings.evidence: va (zap): 'Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set' reported across many endpoints. recon: response did not set content-security-policy. Both agents observed absence of CSP headers.

findings.title: Server version disclosure: Apache httpd 2.4.62 detected
findings.evidence: nmap: http-server-header identified 'Apache/2.4.62 (Debian)'. nmap vulners NSE output includes a cpe for apache:http_server:2.4.62, however live NVD lookup for CVEs failed (NVD query could not be completed), so no NVD CVE was validated for inclusion.

findings.title: ETag header may leak filesystem identifiers (inodes)
findings.evidence: va (nikto): 'Server leaks inodes via ETags' with header fields shown (e.g. '0xW/2700 0x1a17c1c8de4'). nmap also observed an ETag header in responses. Both scanners report ETag content that appears to leak filesystem identifiers.

findings.title: Missing security headers: referrer-policy and strict-transport-security
findings.evidence: recon: response did not set referrer-policy. recon: response did not set strict-transport-security (HSTS). These headers were observed absent in recon's response analysis.

findings.title: Open services and ports discovered (enumeration)
findings.evidence: nmap -sV: open ports detected and services enumerated: tcp/80 (http), tcp/135 (msrpc), tcp/3001 (nessus), tcp/7070 (realserver), tcp/8080 (http/Apache). Port-state NSE output lists many open/filtered ports. This is confirmed service enumeration output from nmap.

correlate.deduplication_notes: Merged multiple overlapping observations: (1) /ftp exposure related items from recon, nikto and zap were combined into a single finding describing the exposed directory and listed files. (2) robots.txt entries and the recon 'Disallow: /ftp' lead were merged into the /ftp finding. (3) CORS issues reported by zap and header findings from nikto were consolidated into one CORS misconfiguration finding. (4) CSP absence reported by both zap and recon were merged into a single CSP missing finding. (5) ETag leakage observations from nikto and nmap were combined. (6) Apache version/service-disclosure and vulners NSE output were grouped into one server-version finding; NVD CVE lookup failed so no CVEs were attached or used to change severity/confidence.
